explanation:
Processor pipelining is a technique used to improve the instruction throughput of a CPU.  Instead of processing one instruction completely before starting the next, pipelining breaks down instruction execution into stages (e.g., fetch, decode, execute, memory, write back).  Each stage processes a different instruction concurrently, increasing the number of instructions completed per clock cycle. This is crucial for performance optimization in modern computer architectures.

Processor pipelining is a technique used to improve the instruction execution rate of a CPU.  Instead of processing one instruction completely before starting the next, pipelining breaks down instruction execution into multiple stages (e.g., fetch, decode, execute, memory access, write back).  Each stage processes a different instruction concurrently, increasing throughput. This is crucial for improving performance in computer systems architecture.
